page.layout: One page of verse, one column of text; running head centred at top; page number top right; a signature mark "D 4" at the foot right of centre. No margin notes.

main_text.p:
Terret caducis, quum ferit arduus
Titanus Ætneos, minásque
Centimanas cohibet Gigantum:

Te perduelli cum grege turpium
Perdet virorum, Barbare, Gallicæ
Fatalis monstrum Gentis, atque
Innocuo rutilans cruore

Immanis, ehen! belIua, quæ bonos
Summi sequentes dogmata Numinis
Virgis cruentas, ine torres,
Et crucibus lacerásque ferro.

Verùm retectis Guisiadum dolis,
Quæ nunc Nauarrum Gallia principem
Virtute sublimi decorum
Marte ferox petit impotente,

Tandem secundo Numine sospitem,
Pacata, iustis reddet honoribus,
Et proximis regi benigna
Sedibus egregium reponet.

Quem nunc cruentis fraudibus explicat,
Et præparatis mortibus eximit,
Cunctisque seruatum periclis
Incolumem fovet aduocata
Christi potentis dextera vindicis.

Hæc sola vires subruit impias.
Hæc tela coniurata rumpit
Sacrilegæ potior caterua,

page.notes: Printed page has a faded show-through of the facing page's text (ghosted letters at top and right), ignored. The word "ehen!" and "belIua" are as far as legible; "ine" in "ine torres" is probably "sine" with the s damaged; "lacerásque" and "fouet" read as printed with some doubt. The text at the top above the running head is show-through and not transcribed.
